source.version: ISCOP 2026 conference poster, one page, PDF posted at cognitive-complexity.net.technion.ac.il/files/2026/02/; no date on the poster itself; read the PDF page (figures and text)
source.title_on_document: The Effects of Human-AI Collaboration on Creativity

paper_design_summary: Two groups of adults (100 did the Forward Association Task, 101 did the Divergent Association Task) did three word-association rounds alone and then three rounds together with an AI agent, in that fixed order. Forward flow (semantic distance between all word pairs in a chain) scores originality, and its standard deviation scores variability, in each round. Before and after the six rounds, participants did the Alternative Uses Task (fluency, and originality scored by the LLM-based CLAUS) and a Semantic Fluency control task.

studies.label: Forward Association Task (FAT) group: solo rounds, then collaborative rounds with an AI agent; AUT pre and post

assignment.what_was_assigned: Nothing is described as randomized. Every participant did the solo rounds first (rounds 1-3) and the collaborative rounds with the AI agent second (rounds 4-6), so AI assistance follows a fixed order. The poster does not say how participants came to do the FAT rather than the DAT.
assignment.quote: HAICCO (left) comprises of participants undergoing either FAT or DAT first on their own (solo; right top) and then with an AI agent (collaborative; right bottom)
assignment.locator: p. 1, Human-AI Creative Collaboration (HAICCO) panel, text at right; round numbers in the 'Study design' figure

arms.name: Solo rounds
arms.description: Rounds 1-3: participant builds the word chain alone

arms.name: Collaborative rounds
arms.description: Rounds 4-6: participant builds the word chain with an AI agent after the solo rounds; these are repeated phases for the same participants, and phase-specific analyzed counts are not stated. The poster does not name the model (p. 1, HAICCO study-design diagram and Results).

participants.exclusions: Not stated; the poster reports completers but gives no exclusions or analyzed counts for the phases or outcomes (p. 1, Participants and Results).
participants.who: 100 participants completed the Forward Association Task (FAT); 60.0 percent female, mean age 43.40 years (SD 13.40). These are reported completers, not an explicitly reported analyzed sample. Recruitment source, country, exclusions, and analysis denominators for each phase and outcome are not stated (p. 1, Participants and Results). Solo and collaborative rounds are repeated phases for the same participants.
participants.quote: 100 participants completed the Forward Association Task (FAT; 60.0% female) with a mean age of 43.40 years (SD = 13.40 years)

ai_tool.how_used: Participant and AI agent build one word chain together in the collaborative rounds; the collaborative example figure shows highlighted words interleaved with the others in the chain.

task.description: Forward Association Task: create a chain of associations, one word at a time; scored by forward flow. AUT (2 minutes, creative uses for an object) and Semantic Fluency Task (2 minutes) before and after the six rounds.

outcomes.name: Forward flow (mean full-chain semantic distance) in the word chain, collaborative vs solo rounds
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Forward flow scores semantic distance between all pairs of words in a chain; the plot reports Full-chain Forward Flow (mean) by task, condition and round. Full-chain SD is recorded separately as a variability outcome (p. 1, HAICCO Tasks and Results).

contrasts.reported: Figure only; no exact numerical outcome estimates or inferential tests are printed, and error bars are not defined. 'Analysis of Mean', FAT panel: y-axis 'Full-chain Forward Flow (mean)', rounds 1-3 within each condition; the collaborative line is above the solo line in every displayed round. Caption: 'Regardless of task, collaborative rounds generates more original responses'.
contrasts.locator: p. 1, Results, 'Analysis of Mean' figure (FAT panel) and caption below the left figures

outcomes.name: AUT originality (CLAUS), post vs pre HAICCO
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: AUT responses receive LLM-based CLAUS originality scores. The poster does not specify whether the plotted originality analysis averages responses per participant or treats individual responses as observations, so the analysis unit is unknown (p. 1, Cognitive Assessment (Pre/Post), AUT description, and Results, AUT CLAUS chart).

contrasts.reported: Figure only; no exact numerical outcome estimates or inferential tests are printed, and error bars are not defined. 'AUT CLAUS' bar chart: the post-HAICCO bar is lower than the pre-HAICCO bar for FAT. Caption: 'Top – regardless of task, AUT fluency (left) increases and originality (right) decreases post-HAICCO'. Conclusions: 'Post HAICCO—regardless of condition—participants exhibit higher fluency and lower originality in the AUT'.
contrasts.locator: p. 1, Results, 'AUT CLAUS' bar chart and caption at right; Conclusions panel

outcomes.name: AUT fluency (number of responses), post vs pre HAICCO
outcomes.question: after_ai

contrasts.reported: Figure only; no exact numerical outcome estimates or inferential tests are printed, and error bars are not defined. 'AUT fluency (n)' bar chart: the post-HAICCO bar is higher than the pre-HAICCO bar for FAT. The accompanying caption states that AUT fluency increases after HAICCO regardless of task (paraphrase).
contrasts.locator: p. 1, Results, 'AUT fluency (n)' bar chart and caption at right

outcomes.name: Full-chain standard deviation (mean), collaborative vs solo rounds
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Separate variability measure plotted as 'Full-chain SD (mean)' under 'Analysis of Standard Deviation'. The poster defines forward flow using semantic distances between word pairs but does not explain the exact full-chain SD calculation, averaging procedure, analysis unit or error bars. It does not define a comparison across different people's outputs; this is not established as across-person diversity (p. 1, HAICCO Tasks and Results).

contrasts.reported: Figure only; no exact numerical outcome estimates or inferential tests are printed, and error bars are not defined. 'Analysis of Standard Deviation', FAT panel: y-axis 'Full-chain SD (mean)', rounds 1-3 within each condition; the collaborative line is above the solo line in every displayed round. This describes the figure and does not establish statistical significance.
contrasts.locator: p. 1, Results, 'Analysis of Standard Deviation' figure (FAT panel) and caption below the left figures; HAICCO Tasks

eligibility.reason: The AI-assistance order is fixed within participants: solo rounds precede collaborative rounds, with AUT assessments before and after HAICCO; allocation to FAT versus DAT is not stated (p. 1, HAICCO text and Study design diagram). Criterion 1 is not met because AI assistance or its order was not randomized; there is no separate group that remains without AI. The poster reports 100 FAT and 101 DAT completers, but no analyzed counts or exclusions, so the analyzed-people threshold is unclear (p. 1, Participants and Results). Criterion 3 is met: forward flow, full-chain SD, AUT fluency and CLAUS originality are scored on produced output (p. 1, HAICCO Tasks, Cognitive Assessment and Results). Core eligibility remains no, with observational context. The poster prints counts, demographics, round numbers and numerical axes, but no exact numerical outcome estimates or inferential tests; error bars are not defined (p. 1, Results).

one_line_finding: In this one-page poster reporting 100 FAT and 101 DAT completers, figures show higher forward flow in later collaborative rounds in both tasks, higher full-chain SD in FAT and lower full-chain SD in DAT, and higher AUT fluency but lower CLAUS originality after HAICCO; exact outcome estimates and inferential tests are not printed (p. 1, Participants, Results and Conclusions).
